Vs.

full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners being plaintiffs filed the original suit for declaration that the kabla deed No.4761 and 4768 dated 11.07.1970 are illegal, fraudulent, collusive and ineffective contending inter-alia that the land of suit holding originally belonged to one Biraj Mistry in 8(eight) anas share and Indu Mistry to the extent of 8 (eight) anas share each. That before C.S. operation Indu Mistry died leaving only son Panchanon and accordingly the C.S. khotian was prepared in the name of Biraj Mistry and Panchanon. Subsequently; Biraj Mistry for want of money with a condition for getting the land back executed and registered two kabla deeds dated 11.07.1970 A.D. in respect of 4.91 acres of land at a consideration of Tk.6,000/-(six thousand) in favour of the principal defendants. The land of homestead and pond with its bank was in khas possession of Biraj Mistry and possession was delivered in respect of "bilan" land. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the 2(two) deeds were written by the deed-writer but the contents of the deeds were not read over to the executant of the deeds. There was an oral agreement that Biraj Mistry or his heirs will borga cultivate the "bilan" land under the principal defendants and the homestead land will be under the control and possession of the executant. Accordingly; Biraj Mistry used to reside in the homestead land and cultivate the bilan land. During liberation war in the year 1971 Biraj Mistry left this country and died in a refujee camp. After liberation of Bangladesh some of the heirs of Biraj Mistry did not return back to this country and the plaintiffs after coming back from India started to reside in the homestead of their grandfather Biraj Mistry and while they wants to cultivate land the defendant took some signatures of them in blank demi papers in order to create a borga contract. The plaintiff No.5 & 6 in good faith signed the papers. Subsequently; on 23rd Paush, 1389 B.S. the defendant No.1-3 disclosed that they will not allow the plaintiff to borga cultivate the "bilan" land and also disclosed to evict the plaintiffs from the homestead. Thereafter; the plaintiffs obtained the certified copies of the disputed kablas & came to learn that the defendants in the kabla deeds fraudulently inserted the homestead land and pond along with its bank. In fact the executant Biraj Mistry never sold out the homestead land, pond and its bank in favour of the defendants. The defendants to grab the valuable property have created the false kabla deeds.
